annotation.title_clean: Japanese and East Asian values as alternative world views with an orientation to plurality of meanings of life in the informatized era: the cultural-ethical traditions behind East Asian people's evaluation on human-robot-interaction, privacy-related problems, AI, Technologies
annotation.title_en: Japanese and East Asian values as alternative world views with an orientation to plurality of meanings of life in the informatized era: the cultural-ethical traditions behind East Asian people's evaluation on human-robot-interaction, privacy-related problems, AI, Technologies
annotation.summary_en: Information-ethics article arguing that informatization erodes plurality of meanings of life, and drawing on Japanese thought (Nishida, Kimura, Seken, Ba) as an alternative world view. It examines how East Asian cultural-ethical traditions shape evaluations of human-robot interaction, privacy and AI, using the author's survey findings.
key_provisions_or_claims: Informatization causes loss of plurality of meanings of life, linked to techno-determinism.
Japanese ontological traditions (Nishida's oneness of meanings, Seken, Ba) offer an alternative world view.
East Asian evaluations of human-robot interaction, privacy and AI are shaped by cultural-ethical traditions.
Intercultural information ethics should be ontology-based, following Capurro.
